character_facts: The human warrior is regarded by the small robot as its master and as an invincible human warrior.
The small robot is highly emotional, dependent on the master's presence, and theatrically distressed by his disappearance.
The larger machine is more controlled and takes the role of correcting the smaller robot and guiding the narration.
characters_present: A bald human warrior identified by the dialogue as the robot's 'master'
Small robot identified by the dialogue as Tonto
continuity_links: This page continues an ongoing embedded account of the origins of the Metabarons.
It directly picks up an earlier interrupted discussion about Othon's mutilation and the conception of the next Metabaron.
dialogue_meaning: The small robot idolizes the human warrior and celebrates his apparent triumph.
The human's sudden disappearance shocks the robot.
The larger machine treats the robot's attachment as foolish sentimentality.
The machines resume a framed storytelling conversation about the ancestry of the Metabarons.
Their immediate topic is the reproductive problem created by Othon's mutilation and prosthetic replacement.
locations: A futuristic mechanical chamber or platform interior with machinery, consoles, and suspended equipment
lore_facts: There is a storytelling frame in which two machines discuss the history or origins of the Metabaron clan.
A figure named Othon is described as having had an essential body part amputated.
Othon is said to have resorted to a multi-protonic pelvic implant.
A central narrative question is how a subsequent Metabaron was conceived despite Othon having no genitals.
The small robot addresses the larger machine as Tonto.
plot_events: A small robot praises its human 'master' after a victory.
The bald armored man reacts briefly and then vanishes or dematerializes in front of the robot.
The small robot panics and laments that the master is gone.
A larger machine rebukes the small robot for becoming emotional and tells it not to delude itself.
The larger machine offers to continue recounting the origins of the Metabarons.
The small robot eagerly agrees and refers back to the unfinished part of the story about Othon's body being mutilated and replaced with an artificial pelvic implant.
The larger machine states that the question at hand is how the next Metabaron could be conceived if Othon had no genitals.
The small robot expresses excited curiosity about how Othon nevertheless fathered a child of his own blood.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the human warrior's disappearance is not explained on the page; he appears to fade out visually.
The precise identity of the bald human warrior is not stated here beyond being called the robot's master.
Some dialogue is small and stylized; while the main meaning is clear, a few exact phrasings may be imperfectly read.
visual_summary: A bald armored man rises from a mechanical chair or cradle while a small robot addresses him admiringly. In the next panels the man fades away until he disappears completely, leaving the robot distressed. A larger floating machine comforts the smaller robot and proposes continuing the story of the Metabarons. The two machines then resume their prior discussion about Othon, his bodily mutilation, and how a later Metabaron could be conceived.
